scales._comment: Tier-scale definitions and the normalization map. Each source declares which scale it uses (sources.json → scale). Values place every tier on one 0–100 axis so sources with different scales can be averaged into a consensus. Consensus bands must be sorted by descending min, ending at 0. 2026-08-14 (owner decision, Riley — applied ahead of the 08-18 flip rather than in the flip commit): the LIVE icyveins scale is now the SAME seven bands as icyveins-ptr. Icy Veins rebuilt its live M+ lists for Midnight Season 2 and they publish S+ and B+, which the old five-band scale could not represent — the merge had been blocked for six days because storing an S+ letter would have failed validation and collapsing it into S was refused as fabrication. The two scales are now identical by intent, not coincidence, so the note below about them deliberately diverging is HISTORY: it described the window when only the PTR list had the extra rungs. Measured on landing: re-spacing S from 100 to 92 re-scores the frozen Season-1 letters the consensus still reads through the frozen lane, moving 13 consensus scores and 3 M+ letters (Unholy DK, Devourer DH, Augmentation Evoker, all S -> A+) — a scale decision, not spec movement, which is why CONSENSUS_VERSION went 3 -> 4 in the same commit. Its shared tiers keep the live anchors exactly (A+ 82 / A 66 / B 48 / C 30) so the same author's live and PTR reads are directly comparable on the axis; B+ sits at 57, the midpoint of A and B. 2026-08-04 (owner decision, Riley): the PTR DPS list added a SEVENTH band, S+, in its 02 Aug. "Update #4" — S+ takes the 100 anchor and S shifts down to 92. This is the one place the PTR scale deliberately stops matching the live one: PTR S is 92 while live S is 100, because the PTR list now reserves a rung above S that the live list has no equivalent for. Collapsing S+ into S was rejected — it would fabricate a placement the source is explicitly distinguishing. Note this re-spacing moves every icyveins-ptr-derived projection input, not just the two S+ specs, since the source feeds projectionFor via ptrTierRead at weight .25 (it is era:ptr, so consensus is untouched).

sources.name: Archon
sources.author: Archon.gg (statistical)
sources.methodology: Statistical tier lists computed from Warcraft Logs parses and Blizzard leaderboards — 14-day rolling window, refreshed daily. Raid tiers read from the throughput metric tier list (NOT the default popularity grouping); M+ tiers from the M+ score tier list. EARLY-S2 BASIS (owner decision 2026-08-25): the raid letters come from the HEROIC throughput list while Mythic is sparse — Heroic carries ~170x the parses and covers all 27 DPS specs where Mythic held 6 specs under 10 parses and no Fire Mage at all. Switch back to the Mythic list (a reviewed registry edit + CONSENSUS_VERSION bump) once Mythic reaches 27/27 DPS with healthy samples. The Mythic rankings pages stay registered as ancillary metric feeds. U.GG has its own methodology and filters; it is not a verified equivalent mirror or replacement feed.
sources.notes: Fetch recipe: parse the __NEXT_DATA__ JSON script tag from raw HTML (WebFetch markdown drops it). Raid pages carry three tierLists (popularity/throughput/survivability) — use metric "throughput"; M+ pages use metric "score". The Heroic raid pages (the letter basis since 2026-08-25) parse with the IDENTICAL recipe — only the /heroic/ path segment differs; the ancillary Mythic rankings pages feed the "(Mythic)" numeric families and survivability. U.GG has its own methodology and filters; it is not a verified equivalent mirror or replacement feed.
sources.summary: Letter grades computed from logged play. Raid tiers come from its THROUGHPUT list and M+ tiers from its SCORE list — never the default popularity grouping, which ranks how often a spec is played rather than how it performs.
